to make (a contract PCB house) Core's board since round 41 (the 30 base), revised by the review of 2026-11-01: a USB PD sink at 9 V on the USB-C path and the dock's pins (an ideal diode on each input); the LTC4162-F LiFePO4 charger with power path (35 V max in), 1.5 A, 3.6 V; a coulomb counter (LTC2941 class [check]) for the gauge and the 90 % stop (4.05 of 4.5 Ah); per cell, back-to-back FETs under an ideal-diode controller (LTC4359 class [check]), off by default; the MCU on a diode-OR of the input and the cells; thermal foldback on a chassis NTC (55 C: LED to 70 %; 60 C: charge to 0.5 A) and the cells' NTC (no charge over 45 C); the warm-dim driver; capacitive touch with baseline tracking and a 50 ms debounce. Laid out as a 48 ring under the LED, the dock's pins on it (the axis and r 20), the USB-C on a flex to its small board in the corner at 170 deg

Nichia or Seoul (to choose) A 30 mm round warm-dim LED board, two channels (2200 K and 2700 K, CRI 90+), 130 lm/W or better: 200 lm at 1.5 W or less (review 2026-11-01; was 2.5 W), on the aluminum chassis's heat path to the touch ring | PROPOSAL (2026-11-03, the Ice night test): warm 2700 K light through Ice glows teal (lit hue -64 deg from its day hue in the render, -36 at 4000 K); it holds within 10 deg only at about 5700 K. So the board's two channels become 2700 K and 5700 K, 95 CRI (tunable white on the same two-channel driver, in place of warm-dim 2200 to 2700 K), and Ice's default is 5700 K. The same 30 mm board family in 5700 K Ra 95 [check: Nichia or Seoul], about the same price ($9 [E]) | THE LED COLOUR PER TINT (the owner, 2026-11-10: "some need warm and some need amber"): amber 2200 K (CRI 90) for Ember; 2700 K for Poison and Fog; 3000 K for Haze; 4000 K for Dust, Acid, Ice and Smoke (the owner, 2026-11-11, on the Core colour test: a dye removes only what the source carries); the same lumens in every bin (Core: the board's bin per tint, the same 200 lm and the same battery)

Power Sonic PSL-FP-IFR18650EC (round 42), three in parallel (1S3P): LiFePO4 18650 energy cell, 3.2 V, 1.5 Ah rated, 4.8 Wh each, 14.4 Wh the set; 2,000 cycles at 100 % depth of discharge; 65 x 18.2 mm (flat top on its datasheet: Core needs a button-top cell for its shrouded + contact, so confirm a button-top version with Power Sonic or qualify another maker [check], review 2026-11-01), about 40 g; charge 3.65 V cut-off, at most 1.5 A (1C); discharge cut-off 2.5 V; charge 0 to 45 C, discharge -20 to 60 C. Approvals on the datasheet: UL 1642 cell certificate, IEC 62133 cell certificate (the edition is not stated: ask Power Sonic for the IEC 62133-2 report), UN 38.3 certified (the test summary, which 49 CFR 173.185(a)(3) requires a cell maker to make available, to request). Each cell 4.8 Wh (at most 20 Wh), the set 14.4 Wh (at most 100 Wh): the small-battery exception (49 CFR 173.185(c), UN3481, contained in equipment)
finish: Capacity confirmed from the datasheet (1.5 Ah). Higher-capacity IFR18650s exist (a Bonrex IFR18650-1.8Ah sheet, 2020) but none found with published IEC 62133 / UN 38.3: Power Sonic's is the certified one
